content: To whom did Paul write his short letter named Philemon?
explanation: Paul wrote as a prisoner. “To Philemon our beloved fellow worker” (Philemon 1:1, BSB)

content: In Philemon, for whom does Paul make his appeal?
explanation: Paul called him his child. “I appeal to you for my child Onesimus” (Philemon 1:10, BSB)

content: In Philemon, Paul asks Philemon to receive Onesimus as a beloved what?
explanation: No longer as a slave. “no longer as a slave, but better than a slave, as a beloved brother.” (Philemon 1:16, BSB)

content: In Philemon, Onesimus was once useless but has now become what?
explanation: His name means useful. “Formerly he was useless to you, but now he has become useful both to you and to me.” (Philemon 1:11, BSB)

content: In Philemon, what did Paul say to do with anything Onesimus owed?
explanation: Paul took on his debt. “But if he has wronged you in any way or owes you anything, charge it to my account.” (Philemon 1:18, BSB)

content: In Philemon, how does Paul describe himself?
explanation: He wrote from chains. “Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus” (Philemon 1:1, BSB)

content: In Philemon, what did Paul ask Philemon to prepare for him?
explanation: He hoped to be released. “In the meantime, prepare a guest room for me” (Philemon 1:22, BSB)

content: In Philemon, whom does Paul call our fellow soldier?
explanation: He was part of the house church. “to Archippus our fellow soldier” (Philemon 1:2, BSB)
